corresponding sound in a projection print. 


2.514 Synchronizing Leader — Length of picture 
consisting of 20 frames a head of picture start marks 
and 12 frames, including picture start mark to 
picture. 


2.515 Synchronizer — Socketed device used for 
synchronizing sound and the related picture used for 
editing films. 


NOTE — This can also be an electronic device used for 
synchronizing processes involved in film production. 


2.516 Tail Leader (Trailer) — Section of film at 
the end of each reel of a film, containing the 
identifying information. 


2.517 Test Films — Films for checking the 
performance of motion picture equipment. 


2.518 Test Print — The first positive to be shown 
to the producers to judge its qualities. 


2.519 Test Shot — Recording made for test 
purposes before the final recording takes place. 


2.520 Textless Background — Picture negative or 
positive, supplied without a title and intended to 
form the background for the title in a foreign 
language edition. 


IS 1885 (Part 34) : 2023 


2.521 Tip-Up Seat — Chair in a theatre the seat of 
which can be titled. 


2.522 Title — Texts or graphics included in the final 
version of the film. 


2.523 Titling — The making and insertion of the 
various titles in the film under manufacture. 


2.524 Trailer — Film on very short footage, 
generally consisting of extracts from a longer film 
and intended to inform the audience of the 
forthcoming presentation of the latter at the cinema. 


2.525 Transfer Loss — The loss in sound quality 
during the copying of the optical sound track. 


2.526 Travel Ghost — The appearance of white 
streaks in all the high lights of the picture due to a 
too early or too late cutting off of the light beam. 


2.527 Travelling Masks — Film rolls used as light 
modulators in printing machines for obtaining 
transitional effects. 


2.528 Under-Development — Time of 


development has been too short. 


2.529 Uniformity Error — Error occurring in film 
perforating machines at the fourth space due to not 
moving the film by the correct amount. 


2.530 Unsteadiness — The presence of undesired 
movement of the image as a whole. 


2.531 Unwinding — Supplying the film from the 
upper magazine into the projector. 


20 


2.532 Unwinding Spool — The spool delivering the 
film to be projected into the projector. 


2.533 Variable Aperture Shutter — Shutter 
allowing for increasing in the depth of field of the 
optical system. 


2.534 Video Tape Recording — Tic art of 
recording pictures on magnetic tape. 


2.535 Weave — Slow, irregular sidewise undesired 
movement of the picture similar to swaying. 


2.536 Wide Angle Lens — Lens having wide angle 
of view, for example picks-up broad area of stage 
setting at short distance. 


2.337 Wide Film — Film the size of which is larger 
than 35 mm. 


2.538 Wipe — Cinematic transition in which the 
new picture starts as small area and grows until it 
covers the whole screen. 


2.539 Working Distance — The distance between 
an object to be taken and the nearest face of a lens in 
the camera. 


2.540 Wow — Effect of the change in pitch due to 
variation in speed in the recording or reproducing 
apparatus. 


2.541 Zoom Lens — A zoom lens is a lens whose 
equivalent focal length can be varied but where 
image plane, for a given object plane, remained at a 
fixed distance from the mounting flange without the 
need for refocusing. 


IS 1885 (Part 34) : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: ETD 01 (21615).
